evidence.note: Explicitly declared a dependency-aware bottom-up order (model → IO → layout → analysis → alignment), calling model 'the foundation for everything else' — genuine sequencing that respects dependencies.
Defined a coherent critical-path milestone: 'SIF parser → default layout → NOA/EDA/BIF output', targeting the simplest test first then expanding — grouping work sensibly with a concrete done-check.
Used specific tests as completion signals (sif_single_node green, then _bif green) before moving to the next chunk — milestone tied to concrete test-green done-checks.
Measured progress by test group (39/85 default_tests) after finishing triangle/gw chunks, confirming an ordered expansion of coverage.

After first tests passed, work became reactive symptom-by-symptom fixing (color order, shadow direction, column values) rather than a maintained milestone map; no explicit tracking (TodoWrite never used despite reminders).

reasoning: The agent clearly exceeds the level-5 anchor: it grouped work sensibly, put foundations (model/IO) before dependents (layout/CLI) with explicit dependency reasoning, and finished coherent chunks (simplest test → BIF → triangle → group) before moving on, using specific test-green done-checks. It reaches into level-8 territory with concrete completion signals sequenced so each unblocks the next and shared primitives built once. But it falls short of a sustained, explicit ordered milestone hierarchy: the map was implicit and restated repeatedly rather than tracked, much of the middle was file-reading thrash, and late work devolved into reactive bug-fixing rather than milestone-driven progression. That places it at a 6, between the 5 and 8 anchors.
